p.src: For now, let us leave Song Jiang's central force crossing the river and speak instead of Beigu Mountain at Runzhou. Lookouts there saw some three hundred warships leave the inlet opposite all at once, flying red vanguard banners proclaiming that they were escorting clothing and provisions. The southern troops hurriedly reported this to the provincial headquarters. Privy Councillor Lü assembled his twelve area commanders. Fully armed and armored, with crossbows strung and blades drawn, they led an elite force to the riverbank to see for themselves. They saw the foremost hundred vessels first draw in close to the bank; looking toward the two leaders aboard and the men crowding around them fore and aft, all wore uniforms of golden chain mail, and every one of them was a burly giant. Privy Councillor Lü dismounted and seated himself upon a silver folding chair, while the twelve area commanders guarded the riverbank in two ranks. When Mu Hong and Li Jun saw Privy Councillor Lü seated on the riverbank, they rose and called out a respectful greeting. The attendants on either side shouted for the ships to halt, and the hundred vessels dropped anchor in a straight line. The two hundred vessels behind them, borne along by a favorable wind, had now all arrived; they divided and drew in from both sides, a hundred to the left and a hundred to the right, forming three evenly arrayed groups. An officer of the guest bureau disembarked and asked, “Where have these ships come from?” Mu Hong replied, “This humble man is Chen Yi, and my younger brother is Chen Tai. Our father, Chen Guan, expressly sent us brothers to present fifty thousand piculs of white rice, three hundred vessels, and five thousand picked soldiers, in gratitude for Your Excellency's kindness in recommending and protecting us.” The guest-bureau officer said, “The other day His Excellency the Privy Councillor sent Attendant Ye to you. Where is he now?” Mu Hong said, “Attendant Ye and Wu Cheng have both contracted a febrile epidemic and are presently recuperating at our estate, so they could not come. Here are the sealed credentials, which we now submit.” The guest-bureau officer received the document, returned to the riverbank, and reported to Privy Councillor Lü: “Chen Yi and Chen Tai, sons of Prefect Chen of Dingpu Village in Yangzhou, have brought grain and offered troops. Here is the sealed document originally carried there, which they have submitted.” Privy Councillor Lü examined it and found that it was indeed the original official document. He issued an order to summon the two men ashore. The guest-bureau officer summoned Chen Yi and Chen Tai to come forward and pay their respects. Mu Hong and Li Jun came ashore, and twenty deputy generals followed behind them. The guards shouted, “His Excellency is here! No unauthorized persons may approach!” The twenty deputy generals all stopped where they were. Mu Hong and Li Jun bowed with clasped hands and stood waiting at a distance. Only after a long while did the guest-bureau officer lead one man forward. He paid homage and knelt before the councillor. Privy Councillor Lü asked, “Why did your father, Chen Guan, not come in person?” Mu Hong reported, “My father heard that Song Jiang and the others from Liangshan Marsh were approaching with an army. Fearing that the bandits might descend upon the countryside and cause trouble, he remained at home to deal with them and dared not leave without permission.” Privy Councillor Lü asked, “Which of you two is the elder brother?” Mu Hong replied, “Chen Yi is the elder.” Privy Councillor Lü asked, “Have you brothers ever trained in the martial arts?” Mu Hong replied, “Thanks to Your Excellency's gracious protection, we have had a fair amount of training.” Privy Councillor Lü asked, “How is the white grain you brought loaded?” Mu Hong replied, “The large vessels carry three hundred piculs of grain each, and the small ones two hundred.” Privy Councillor Lü said, “I fear that you two have come with some hidden purpose!” Mu Hong replied, “My father and we his sons are wholly devoted in our loyalty. How would we dare harbor the slightest ulterior motive?” Privy Councillor Lü said, “Though your intentions may be good, the soldiers aboard your ships look most extraordinary. One cannot help but be suspicious. You two will remain here. I shall send four area commanders with a hundred soldiers to search the ships. If they find anything out of the ordinary, you will certainly not be spared.” Mu Hong said, “This humble man came hoping that Your Excellency would entrust him with important service. Why must you suspect us?” Just as Lü Shinang was about to select four area commanders to search the vessels, a mounted scout came with a report:

p.src: Now Privy Councillor Lü reached the southern gate and received the imperial envoy. He immediately asked, “Why have you come with such urgency?” The imperial envoy was Feng Xi, Fang La's usher. He whispered to Lü Shinang, “Recently, Pu Wenying, the court eunuch of the Bureau of Astronomy, memorialized: ‘Observing the heavens by night, I saw countless stars of the Heavenly Spirits enter the celestial region corresponding to Wu. Half among them were dim, yet the calamity hidden therein will be no small matter.’ His Majesty has therefore issued a special edict ordering Your Excellency to guard the riverbank closely. Anyone arriving from the north must be carefully questioned and interrogated until the truth is known; if any appear strange or suspicious, execute them at once and suffer no delay.” Privy Councillor Lü was greatly alarmed on hearing this. “I was deeply suspicious of that band just now, and here comes this warning. For now, please come into the city, where we shall open and proclaim the edict.” Feng Xi and Privy Councillor Lü went together to the provincial headquarters, where the edict was opened and proclaimed. No sooner was this done than another rider galloped in to report, “Another envoy has come from Suzhou, bearing an order from His Highness the Third Prince, the Emperor's younger brother.” It said, “The recent matter of the surrender of the Chen commanders from Yangzhou must not yet be trusted, for I fear there may be deceit. We have lately received an imperial edict stating that the Bureau of Astronomy has observed men corresponding to the stars of the Heavenly Spirits within the celestial region of Wu. You must therefore guard the riverbank securely. I shall soon send men of my own to supervise you.” Privy Councillor Lü said, “His Highness too is concerned about this matter. This humble official has already received the imperial edict.” He immediately ordered the river closely guarded: not a single person aboard the arriving ships was to be allowed ashore. At the same time, he laid a banquet to entertain the two envoys.

p.src: Now the men aboard those three hundred ships, seeing no sign of movement for half the day, began to act. From the hundred ships on the left, Zhang Heng and Zhang Shun led eight junior generals ashore, weapons in hand; from the hundred ships on the right, ten senior generals seized their spears and sabres and scrambled ashore. The southern troops guarding the riverfront could not hold them back. Li Kui the Black Whirlwind, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao charged straight into the city. The government soldiers guarding the gate rushed out to intercept them. Li Kui swung his twin axes, hewing and hacking, and in an instant struck down two of the gate guards. A great cry arose by the walls. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao each levelled a steel fork and stormed into the city; with everyone springing into action at once, how could the gates possibly be shut in time? Li Kui planted himself beneath the gateway, seeking men to hack down. The twenty junior generals who had reached the walls first each seized a weapon and joined the slaughter. Privy Councillor Lü hurriedly sent orders that the riverfront be stoutly defended, but by then the enemy had already fought their way through the gate and into the city. When the twelve commanders heard the shouting by the walls and each began mobilizing his troops, Shi Jin and Chai Jin had already rallied the soldiers aboard the three hundred ships. Casting off their southern-army uniforms, they led the way ashore, and all the troops concealed in the holds surged onto the bank together. When the chief commanders Shen Gang and Pan Wende brought two columns to defend the gate, Shi Jin hacked Shen Gang from his horse with one stroke, while Zhang Heng thrust in obliquely and ran Pan Wende through with his spear. Amid the general melee, the remaining ten commanders all retreated into the inner city to protect their families. When Mu Hong and Li Jun heard the news inside the city, they seized fire from an inn and began setting the city ablaze. Just as Privy Councillor Lü was hastily mounting his horse, three commanders arrived to aid him. Flames seemed to rain from heaven throughout the city. Seeing this from Guazhou, the defenders there immediately dispatched a force of troops to come to their aid. After fierce fighting had raged for a long while at all four gates, Commander Song's banners were already flying above the walls. Men and horses fought in confusion on every side; the full tale cannot be told here, but what followed will soon be seen.

p.src: Meanwhile, on the north bank of the river, one hundred and fifty warships had already drawn alongside the shore. The horses were all led ashore, and ten leading generals landed in full battle array. Those ten great generals—Guan Sheng, Huyan Zhuo, Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Hao Siwen, Xuan Zan, Shan Tinggui, Han Tao, Peng Qi, and Wei Dingguo—led one thousand senior and junior officers and two thousand troops in a charge into the city. By then Privy Councillor Lü had suffered a crushing defeat and fled straight to Dantu County with his wounded men and horses. Having captured Runzhou, the main army first ordered the fires extinguished and posted detachments at all four gates. They then returned to the riverbank to welcome Commander Song's ships, and saw the dragon-like and whale-like vessels riding the fair wind across the river, all arriving at the southern bank. Officers great and small welcomed Commander Song into the city. Proclamations were posted in advance to reassure the people, and the officers of his command were mustered to report at headquarters and claim merit. Shi Jin presented Shen Gang's head; Zhang Heng presented Pan Wende's; Liu Tang presented Shen Ze's. Kong Ming and Kong Liang captured Zhuo Wanli alive; Xiang Chong and Li Gun captured He Tong alive; and Hao Siwen shot Xu Tong dead with an arrow. Thus Runzhou was taken: four commanders were slain, two captured alive, and staff officers and soldiers killed beyond all count.

p.src: When Song Jiang mustered the officers under his command, he found that three junior generals had been lost, killed amid the confusion by arrows or trampled beneath horses. The three were Song Wan, the Vajra in the Clouds; Jiao Ting, the Unpresentable; and Tao Zongwang, the Nine-Tailed Turtle. The loss of the three generals filled Song Jiang with grief, and he remained downcast and joyless. Wu Yong consoled him: “The bounds of life and death are ordained. Though we have lost three brothers, we should rejoice that we have taken the first great strategic stronghold south of the Yangtze. Why grieve and thereby injure your precious health? If we are to render service to the realm, I beg you first to attend to our weighty affairs.” Song Jiang said, “The one hundred and eight of us are recorded in the patterns of heaven, each corresponding to a star. When we first made our vow at Liangshan Marsh and later swore our oath on Mount Wutai, our sole wish was to live and die together. Yet after we returned to the capital, who could have imagined that Gongsun Sheng would leave us first, that Jin Dajian and Huangfu Duan would be retained at court, that Grand Preceptor Cai would employ Xiao Rang, and that Commandant Wang would request Yue He? Today, scarcely had we crossed the river when I lost three more brothers. When I think of Song Wan, though he never performed any extraordinary feat, we owed him much when Liangshan Marsh was first founded. And today he has become a dweller beneath the springs!” Song Jiang gave orders for the soldiers to erect an altar where Song Wan had died. They laid out spirit money and set forth a black pig and a white sheep, and Song Jiang personally performed the rites and poured the libation. The captured rebel commanders Zhuo Wanli and He Tong were brought there under guard and beheaded; their blood was offered in sacrifice to the heroic spirits of the three fallen men. Song Jiang returned to the prefectural offices and distributed rewards for merit. At the same time, he drew up an official report and sent a man to inform and invite Pacification Commissioner Zhang. Of this there is no more to say. All the corpses strewn along the streets were gathered, carried outside the city, and burned. The remains of the three junior generals were recovered and buried beyond the eastern gate of Runzhou.

p.src: Meanwhile, Privy Councillor Lü, having lost more than half his forces, withdrew with six commanders to defend Dantu County. How could he dare advance again? He sent an urgent appeal to Suzhou, reporting the crisis to Third Prince Fang Mao and begging for aid. Presently a scout came to report that Suzhou had dispatched Marshal Xing Zheng at the head of an army and that he had arrived. Privy Councillor Lü received Marshal Xing and exchanged greetings with him. Upon reaching the county offices, he related in full how General Chen had feigned surrender and thereby allowed Song Jiang's army to cross the river undetected. “Now that you have arrived, Marshal, we can recover Runzhou together.” Xing Zheng replied, “Third Prince Fang Mao learned that the Stars of the Dipper were invading the land of Wu, and therefore specially dispatched me with an army to patrol and guard the riverfront. I did not expect Your Excellency to suffer defeat. I shall avenge you, and you must support me in battle.” The next day, Xing Zheng led his army forth to retake Runzhou.

p.src: Meanwhile, Song Jiang was consulting with Wu Yong in the yamen at Runzhou. He sent Tong Wei and Tong Meng with more than a hundred men to Jiaoshan to seek Shi Xiu and Ruan Xiaoqi, while at the same time mobilizing troops to march from the city and seize Dantu County. He selected five thousand troops and appointed ten senior generals to lead them. The ten were Guan Sheng, Lin Chong, Qin Ming, Huyan Zhuo, Dong Ping, Hua Rong, Xu Ning, Zhu Tong, Suo Chao, and Yang Zhi. The ten senior generals thereupon led five thousand picked troops out of Runzhou and advanced toward Dantu County. As Guan Sheng and the others marched on, they encountered Xing Zheng's army coming toward them on the road. The two armies faced each other, loosed arrows to hold the opposing line in check, and drew up their battle formations. From the southern army's ranks, Xing Zheng rode out with his spear levelled, while the six commanders took their places on either flank. Seeing him from the Song army's ranks, Guan Sheng spurred forth, brandishing his Green Dragon Crescent Blade, and engaged Xing Zheng. The two generals fought for fourteen or fifteen bouts, until one of them wheeled and fell from his horse. Indeed, the earthen jar is always broken beside the well, and the general is destined to die before the battle line. Which of the two generals was defeated in their fierce combat? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.

As Guan Sheng and the others marched on, they encountered Xing Zheng's army coming toward them on the road.
The two armies faced each other, loosed arrows to hold the opposing line in check, and drew up their battle formations.
From the southern army's ranks, Xing Zheng rode out with his spear levelled, while the six commanders took their places on either flank.

ja: せいりゅうえんげつとう
u.src: Seeing him from the Song army's ranks, Guan Sheng spurred forth, brandishing his Green Dragon Crescent Blade, and engaged Xing Zheng.
The two generals fought for fourteen or fifteen bouts, until one of them wheeled and fell from his horse.
Indeed, the earthen jar is always broken beside the well, and the general is destined to die before the battle line.
Which of the two generals was defeated in their fierce combat? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
